why: Every string the shell, navigation, tab bar and primary actions are made of, in one file, for three apps. Until this contract existed the same table was typed out three times — TypeScript, Swift, Kotlin — and held together by a check that asked only whether each file mentioned each locale code. That check could not see a key translated on Android and forgotten on iOS, which is the drift that actually happens. The table is generated now, so the drift has nowhere to come from, and the check reads this file instead of guessing at three others.
honesty: South Africa has twelve official languages. MyThuso is not able to translate a health service into eleven of them properly, and pretending otherwise is the dangerous option: a confidently wrong sentence in a language the reader trusts is worse than an honest note that nobody has checked it. So every locale carries the state of its review, the app shows that state to the reader in the language dialog, and scripts/check-boundaries.mjs fails the build if a locale claims a human review without naming the person who did it and the day they did it.

clinicalRule.sentence: Clinical wording stays in English until a clinician who reads the language has reviewed it. A reference range, a dose, an observation label and a refusal sentence from a clinical contract are shown in English in every locale below, because a mistranslated instruction is a safety problem rather than a polish problem.
clinicalRule.mechanism: This is structural rather than a promise. No clinical string has a key in this file, so there is nothing for a translator to fill in; clinicalLocale() on all three platforms returns en-ZA for every locale whose clinicalReview state is not "complete"; and the build fails if any string here matches a sentence held in a clinical contract, or if a locale claims a completed clinical review without naming the clinician and their registration.
clinicalRule.refusal: This part of the app is in English. It has not been reviewed by a clinician who reads your language, and a health instruction nobody has checked is not safer for being in your language.

reviewStates.label: Source language
reviewStates.detail: Everything is written in English first. There is nothing to review it against.

reviewStates.label: Checked by a person
reviewStates.detail: A named person who speaks the language read every string and signed the review. A locale may only claim this state with a name, an organisation and a date in this file, and the build fails without them.

reviewStates.label: Machine-drafted · awaiting review
reviewStates.notice: Drafted by software and not yet checked by a person who speaks it. Words on this screen may be wrong. Anything clinical stays in English.
reviewStates.detail: Drafted by software. Nobody who speaks the language has read it. It is shown because a reader who is offered nothing in their language is worse served than a reader who is offered a draft and told it is one — but it is labelled everywhere it appears.

sets.name: The shell
sets.detail: Navigation, the tab bar, the greeting, the preview notices and the primary calls to action. Every locale carries this set in full; a locale that cannot is not offered.

sets.name: The hero banner
sets.detail: The three landing slides and the headline copy. Marketing prose, and the hardest thing to draft without a speaker of the language, so a locale may carry the shell without carrying this.

sets.name: Workspace entries
sets.detail: The vetting console shell and the way into the patient file, the consultation record, the household record and the health summary. The way in is navigation and is translated; what is inside them is the clinical contracts speaking and is not.

fallback: A key a locale does not carry is rendered in English, never blank and never as its own key name. A locale that carries only the shell shows an English hero banner and an English vetting console, and says so in the language dialog rather than letting the reader discover it.

review.note: Drafted without a speaker of the language in the room. The four languages that predate this file are in the same state as the seven added with it: no review was ever recorded for them, so none is claimed.

signLanguage.name: South African Sign Language
signLanguage.status: South Africa’s twelfth official language, added to section 6(1) of the Constitution by the Constitution Eighteenth Amendment Act, 2023.
signLanguage.whyNotInTheList: SASL is a visual language with its own grammar and no written form. It is not English on the hands, and there is nothing to put in the table above. Offering it beside isiZulu and Afrikaans as a language the interface is translated into would be a lie — a reader would choose it and nothing on the screen would change. It is offered instead as a communication requirement that travels with the account, and the interface stays in whichever written language the person chooses separately.

requirement.label: I use South African Sign Language
requirement.detail: A qualified SASL interpreter is arranged for every visit and every call, at no cost to you. Your written language stays whatever you chose above.
requirement.cost: Never charged for. An accommodation that is billed is a fee for being Deaf.

mustHappen.title: The booking will not complete without an interpreter
mustHappen.sentence: When the account records this requirement, a visit is not offered at a time no interpreter is available. It is offered at the next time one is, with the wait shown, because a slot booked without an interpreter is a visit that will fail on the doorstep.

mustHappen.title: The nurse knows before she leaves
mustHappen.sentence: The dispatch note says the patient signs, that an interpreter is arranged, and how the interpreter will be present. It says nothing else about the patient’s hearing, because how much somebody hears is a clinical fact and the dispatch note is not a clinical record.

mustHappen.title: The interpreter is on the roster, named and consented to
mustHappen.sentence: A SASL interpreter joins a teleconsultation as the interpreter already on the call roster — named, bound by the same confidentiality as the clinicians, and asked about like everybody else. There is no second, quieter mechanism for adding one.

mustHappen.title: Sound only is not a degraded call, it is no call at all
mustHappen.sentence: The connection ladder treats sound only as a designed path. For a patient who signs it is not a path: the picture is the language. A call that drops to sound only is rebooked, not continued.

mustHappen.title: Anything written is offered as well, never instead
mustHappen.sentence: A written summary is offered in addition to the interpretation and only if the patient wants one. It is never the way the consultation is conducted.

mustHappen.title: The requirement lives on the account
mustHappen.sentence: It is established once and travels with every booking. A Deaf patient does not explain themselves again at each visit.

mustNeverHappen.sentence: A family member is never used as the interpreter for a clinical conversation. Not a spouse, not an adult child, not a neighbour who signs a little. A person who is part of the story cannot be the channel it is told through, and a child interpreting a diagnosis for a parent is a harm the appointment caused.

A Deaf patient is never written to in English and assumed to have understood. English is a second language for many Deaf South Africans and SASL is their first. A nod is not comprehension, and neither is a signature.
Lip-reading is never counted as an accommodation the service provided. It is something a patient may choose to do; it is not something MyThuso may rely on.
SASL is never listed as a language the interface is translated into. There is no written SASL to translate into, and a language toggle that changes nothing is a claim of access rather than access.
An interpreter is never added to a call or a visit without being named to the patient and consented to first, on the same roster as everybody else who can see and hear them.
A visit is never dispatched without the interpreter on the grounds that the nurse will manage. Managing is what happens instead of a consultation.

teleconsult.sentence: The interpreter is the participant the call roster already has. When this requirement is on the account that participant becomes essential: the call does not open without them, and declining them rebooks the consultation rather than continuing it in a language the patient did not choose — which is what the roster already says happens.

signLanguage.notYetBuilt: None of this is a working service. There is no interpreter roster, no interpreter vetting row and no scheduling that can hold a visit until one is free. What exists is the requirement, the refusals it creates, and the place each of them belongs. An interpreter is a vetted party who hears a whole consultation, and the vetting table does not have a row for one yet.
